newsitem.title: GERMANY: ZMP sees pressure on German new crop wheat prices.
newsitem.headline: ZMP sees pressure on German new crop wheat prices.

text.p: Prices of German new crop wheat are likely to slide due to a weaker price environment in the rest of Europe, farm price office ZMP said in a weekly report.
Consumers were well covered, ample crops were in the pipeline and remaining volumes from the 1996 harvest were finding their way into intervention stores, it said.
"These intervention offers will dampen producers' hopes that pre-harvest contracts will be fixed near the prices seen ahead of the 1996 crop," it said.
The May intervention buying-level for all grains is just 248.61 marks/tonne while nominal fob levels quoted for spot old crop wheat hold at 280-315 marks.
A year ago, spot old crop cost 325-345 marks fob.
ZMP said unmarketable wheat from the Schleswig-Holstein, Lower Saxony and Bavaria states may be offered into public stocks this week, the last in the November-May intervention season.
The European Union's decision on May 14 to impose 15 ecus a tonne on daily exports of soft wheat had effectively reduced internal prices.
Rains on formerly drought-stressed EU crops were also bearish and United States winter wheat output was shaping up well, in contrast to earlier frost damage forecasts.
But the ZMP report stressed wheat prices were not headed for a free fall because world supply was not that ample.

The EU was within its right to cut or abolish the wheat export tax or return to subsidies in its arrangements for new crop wheat sales, which may be tendered from as early as end-May/early June, it argued.
According to the International Grains Council (IGC), global wheat markets were forecast to show a small supply deficit in 97/98 and carry-in stocks had also been cut by the IGC.
Germany's wheat area was projected to increase by four percent to 2.7 million hectares but areas in Denmark, the Benelux countries and Spain were forecast to fall.
Before the most recent price falls, the 96/97 season had featured active EU exports and higher domestic wheat use in the EU, all leading to an overall tight supply scenario, ZMP said.
EU wheat use in feed had risen to 37.50 million tonnes from 34.60 million while industrial uses and exports were also up.
